members.summary: int8-weight linear with per-forward dynamic activation quantization.
members.extended:
Dynamic quantization keeps the weight permanently in int8 (per-output-channel
symmetric) while the activation grid is derived from the *live* input on every
forward — the input's min/max are measured, it is fake-quantized to a per-tensor
affine grid, and the ordinary linear op then runs in float with the dequantized
weight.  Because no representative data is needed to fix the activation range,
this layer needs no calibration pass, which makes it the standard choice for
Transformer / Linear-heavy inference (BERT and friends).  Instances are produced
by `lucid.quantization.quantize_dynamic`, not constructed directly.

parameters.name: in_features
parameters.description: Size of each input sample — the weight's input dimension.

parameters.name: out_features
parameters.description: Size of each output sample — the weight's output dimension.

parameters.name: bias
parameters.description: If `True`, keep a learned float bias buffer; otherwise no bias is added.

notes:
The weight lives in the `weight_int8` buffer alongside per-channel
`weight_scale` / `weight_zero_point`; only the int8 form is the persistent,
device-tracked state, and the float weight is reconstructed on demand.

members.summary: int8-weight GRU built from a float `lucid.nn.GRU`.
members.extended:
The GRU counterpart of `LSTM`: each layer's (and direction's)
`weight_ih` / `weight_hh` is stored int8 per-row symmetric under the
flat name a float GRU's `state_dict` uses (`weight_ih_l0_int8`,
`weight_ih_l0_scale`), the biases stay float, and a float `nn.GRU`
shell outside the module registry runs the recurrence on the dequantized
weights.  Built by `lucid.quantization.quantize_dynamic`.

parameters.name: shell
parameters.description: The float GRU whose configuration and recurrence are reused.

members.summary: int8-weight LSTM built from a float `lucid.nn.LSTM`.
members.extended:
A dynamically quantized recurrent layer: every recurrent weight matrix
(`weight_ih_l*` / `weight_hh_l*`) is stored int8 (per-row symmetric) while
the biases stay float.  A float `nn.LSTM` *shell*, held outside the module
registry so its float weights never enter the `state_dict`, is the actual
compute engine — on each forward its weights are overwritten with the values
dequantized from the int8 buffers, so only the int8 form is the persistent,
device-tracked state.  No calibration is required; the per-timestep activation
quantization inside the cell is left to the real low-precision kernel.  Build
instances with `lucid.quantization.quantize_dynamic`, the recommended
path for LSTM-heavy inference.

parameters.name: shell
parameters.description:
The float LSTM whose configuration and cell arithmetic are reused; it holds
the recurrent weights that `from_float` quantizes to int8.

notes:
The shell is stored via `object.__setattr__` so it stays out of the module
registry, keeping the serialized state limited to the int8 weight buffers, the
per-row scales, and the float biases.

members.summary: int8-weight Elman cell built from a float `lucid.nn.RNNCell`.
members.extended:
Stored and run like `LSTMCell`, with a float `nn.RNNCell`
shell, so its `nonlinearity` (`tanh` or `relu`) is kept.  Built by
`lucid.quantization.quantize_dynamic`.

parameters.name: shell
parameters.description: The float cell whose configuration and arithmetic are reused.

extended:
Weights are quantized to int8 ahead of time; **activations are quantized
per-forward** from their observed range (no calibration data needed).  This
is the go-to for Linear-heavy / Transformer inference, produced by
`lucid.quantization.quantize_dynamic`.
